To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
cooperative hydrogen bonding of an electrophilic barbiturate dye with a pyridine derivative enhances both Lewis acidity and nucleophilicity.

the supramolecular assembly of the electrophilic barbiturate dye with 2,6-di-acetamidopyrimidine enhances its electrophilicity, as shown by a marked increase of both its Lewis acidity and electophilicity.
cooperative hydrogen bonding can enhance the reactivity of an electrophilic barbiturate dye by increasing both Lewis acidity and the electrophilicity.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the design and synthesis of supramolecular complexes that are capable of cooperative hydrogen bonding.
the design of supramolecular systems that can be tuned to exhibit specific chemical and physical properties.
the development of new molecular materials with enhanced properties by supramolecular interactions.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that

cooperative hydrogen bonding of the barbituric acid derivative 2a to the diacetamidopyridines 1a and 1b results in a significant increase in the Lewis acidity and electophilicity of the barbiture moiety, which is reflected by an increase of the reactivity towards nucleophiles.
the supramolecular complex of 2,6-di-acetamidopyrimidine and 5,5'-dibromo-2,2'-bithiobarbituric acid is a more reactive electrophile than the free 5,5'dibromo-2,-2'-bithibabituric acid.
the supramolecular complex of the highly dipolar barbeturate and 2, 6-diacetaminopyridine is a cooperative hydrogen bonded complex, and the hydrogen bonding is a cooperative one.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
cooperative hydrogen bonding can be an effective strategy to enhance the reactivity of a dye.
the cooperative hydrogen bonding of the barbituric acid dye 1 with 2,6-di(acetamidopyrimidine) (DAP) enhances the reactivity of 1 towards cyanide by a factor of 10.

the supramolecular complex formed between the barbiturate and the hydrogen bond donor is more reactive in the reaction with cyanide than the free dye, and that this increase in reactivity is a consequence of a cooperative effect of hydrogen bonding.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the supramolecular complex of a dipolar barbituric acid with a pyridyl derivative is a powerful tool for tuning the reactivity of electrophiles.
cooperative hydrogen bonding can be a powerful means to modulate the reactivity of organic dyes.
the supramolecular complex is not only more reactive but also more selective.
